content: A functional murmur, also referred to as an innocent murmur or physiologic murmur, is a type of heart murmur that arises primarily due to physiological conditions external to the heart, rather than structural abnormalities within the heart itself. It is important to note that serious medical conditions can still develop even in the absence of a primary structural defect in the heart. Peripheral conditions may also contribute to the generation of cardiac abnormalities. Therefore, the use of terms such as innocent or benign should be approached with caution in this context. Innocent murmurs are generally inconsequential and tend to resolve as the child grows older. The physical examination of a functional murmur reveals several characteristic features: 1. The murmur is soft, with an intensity of less than 3/6. However, it is important to recognize that the intensity of a murmur does not necessarily correlate with the severity of an underlying structural heart disease, if present. 2. The murmur is often position-dependent. It is typically heard when the patient is in a supine position and may disappear when the patient is upright or sitting. 3. The murmur occurs during systole or may persist continuously during both systole and diastole. It is critical to note that murmurs occurring exclusively during diastole are always considered pathologic. 4. Physiologic splitting of the second heart sound (S2) is often observed. The A2 (aortic) and P2 (pulmonic) components of S2 should only be distinguishable during inspiration and should merge during expiration.
